rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 <U+2013> own UAV multispectral flights (four dates, 2017-2019) over three olive groves in Apulia, visual severity scoring of each tree quadrant (4095 observations), polygon cokriging and parametric/non-parametric discriminant analysis with cross-validation (Tables 5-8).
rows.notes: The study only shows that UAV multispectral data combined with geostatistics and discriminant analysis can classify olive-tree quadrants into early/asymptomatic vs symptomatic Xfp severity classes (non-parametric cross-validation overall accuracy 0.69; class 0 accuracy 0.77). It reports no result on controlling or limiting the spread of Xylella; the link from detection to control is asserted in the Introduction/Discussion (maps could direct scouting and sampling), not demonstrated. Detection is a precondition of the claimed control effect, so Q2 is no and upstream is true. Note also that detection relies on visual symptoms (>5% wilting threshold), not the latent pre-symptomatic stage.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 <U+2013> own UAV flights, visual disease ratings and discriminant classification with cross-validation (Tables 5-8); prediction for eight unrated trees in Torchiarolo with posterior probabilities (Figure 10).
rows.notes: The study demonstrates monitoring/classification of Xfp symptom severity with UAV imagery and describes temporal evolution of stressed trees across flights (Figure 8), but it does not report any result on prevention or management strategies being adopted or on their outcome. The Discussion proposes that canonical-variable maps and posterior probabilities could be used as a decision-support tool to prioritise scouting and molecular diagnosis; this is a recommendation, not an own finding. Monitoring is a precondition of the claimed management effect, so Q2 is no and upstream is true.

notes: Full text available; supplementary variogram figures not included but not needed. The study is a methodological detection/classification paper; both claim rows concern pest control/management, which the study does not test.
